title: Separate portable output from governed recording

statement: The system shall support the selected capability's authorized portable output without CLI recording, and shall activate the complete supported recording procedure when a governed or durable-recording trigger applies, preserving exact scope, explicit decisions, conflict handling, and truthful recording results.

what.problem: Always requiring recording prevents legitimate portable use, while silently remaining portable after a governed trigger omits required evidence and scope controls.
what.desired_outcome: Participants receive a valid portable result or a correctly bounded governed recording result under the selected capability contract.

why.rationale: Optional adoption of record tooling must coexist with complete recording duties wherever the project requires them.

conditions: At invocation classification, a late governed or durable trigger, and before any required record read or write.

contexts: The selected capability path in the participant's project context.

how.approach: Identify portable versus governed obligations from the actual capability and project context. Load the applicable supported CLI procedure when required, prepare explicit scope and decisions, inspect operation results, and handle conflicts without treating persistence as approval.

how_much.scope: The common boundary between published guidance and the currently supported CLI. Current stored-format details, selectors, revision identities, atomicity and recovery remain with CLI/Records; this draft introduces no new command or record version and no fallback from malformed governed context to ungoverned writes.

acceptance_criteria: An authorized portable invocation can produce its supported artifact or advisory result without a CLI or change record and makes no governed completion claim.

A governed or durable trigger, including one discovered late, activates the complete applicable recording procedure before dependent action; missing authority, resources, or CLI support results in an explicit stop.
Recording requests use current supported commands and selectors with explicit target, scope, applicable read or revision identity, and actor-owned decisions; the agent inspects actual results.
A conflict, interruption, or unexpected response is handled through the current owner's recovery procedure, preserving existing records and historical meaning without an invented success claim.
Successful recording establishes only the observed persistence outcome; it grants neither assessment approval nor permission to continue or publish.
